<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. XX.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 AND <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>th. 21.23. Mark. 11.27.</ns0:note> it came pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> with the elders.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 4.7. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 7.27.</ns0:note> By what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?<ns0:note place="bottom">We have along the History of the Gospel observed, that the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> took all advantages imaginable against our Saviour; failing in all their acts they now come to question his Authority, which seemeth not so much to have respect to his Preaching, as to his act in casting of the <ns0:hi>Buyers</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sellers out of the Temple,</ns0:hi> for as to <ns0:hi>Preaching,</ns0:hi> they seemed by the History of Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture to have given a great liberty, especially if any had the repute of a Prophet.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And he answered, and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And they reasoned with themselves, saying, if we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be perswaded that John was a pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And they answered, that they could not tell whence <ns0:hi>it was.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And Jesus said unto them, Nether tell<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> you by what authority I do these things.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.24, 25. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 11.28, 29. The substance of our Saviours answer is this. From whence had <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> his Authority? he <ns0:hi>Preached,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Baptized,</ns0:hi> who gave him his Authority? They had sent much such another Message to <ns0:hi>Iohn, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.21, 22, 23. was <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Authority <ns0:hi>ordinary</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>extraordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nary</ns0:hi>? It is plain that he had no Authority from them, for then they would not have sent to him to know <ns0:hi>who he was.</ns0:hi> He must therefore have it from Heaven, now if they had allowed <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s call extroardinary, why should not they allow Christs to be such, to whom <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> gave so large a testimony, and who confirmed his extroardinary M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ssion by Miraculous Operations, which we do not read that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> ever did? Besides the Pharisees saw that if they allowed <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s Mission to be extraordinary, and from Heaven, they had obviously exposed themselves to a check, for not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving what he said, they therefore refuse to make any answer, and Christ refuseth also to satisfie them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Then began he to speak to the people this para<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble: A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And at the season he sent a servant to the hus<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> away empty.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And again he sent another servant; and they beat him also, and entreated <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> shamefully, and sent <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> away empty.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And again he sent the third; and they wound<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed him also, and cast <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> out.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Then said the Lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> when they see him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 But when the husbandmen saw him, they rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed <ns0:hi>him.</ns0:hi> What therefore shall the lord of the vine<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yard do unto them?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they said, God forbid.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is writen, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Math. 21.42.</ns0:note> The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Whosoever shall fall upon that stone, shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.<ns0:note place="bottom">We met with this <ns0:hi>Parable</ns0:hi> at large both in <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.33. to the end, and in <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 12.1. Its obvious Scope is to let them know, that God in righteous Judgment, for the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> abusing the <ns0:hi>Lord</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Prophets, Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> and himself, who was in a few Days to be killed by them, would unchurch and destroy them, and raise up to himself a Church amongst the Gentiles, and that this was no more then was Prophecied of, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 118.22<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:321" />
the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And they watched <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and sent forth spies, which should <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Math. 22.15.20.</ns0:note> feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they mig<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                     <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> deliver him unto the power and authority of the go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vernour.<ns0:note place="bottom">There is nothing in these verses, but what we before met with, and is opened in the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.45, 46. or <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 12.12, 13. They let us see as in a Glass <ns0:hi>the Spirit,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Genius</ns0:hi> of Wick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Men filled with <ns0:hi>Malice</ns0:hi> against the <ns0:hi>Gospel.</ns0:hi> They are conti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nually seeking to destroy such as have any relation to Christ, and to effect their ends, they will judge no means unfair, and their great art is to represent them as dangerous Persons to the <ns0:hi>Civil Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vernment,</ns0:hi> so as if good Men find the same things still, they have this to comfort them, <ns0:hi>That the Disciple is not above his Master, nor the Servant above his Lord.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither accept<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est thou the person <ns0:hi>of any,</ns0:hi> but teachest the way of God <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>of a Truth.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> truly.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Cesar, or no?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Shew me a <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Matth. 18.28.</ns0:note> penny: Whose image and super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scription hath it? They answered and said, Cesars.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Cesar the things which be Cesars, and unto God the things which be Gods.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And they could not take hold of his words be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.<ns0:note place="bottom">This piece of History we have likewise met with both, in <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 22.16. and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 12.13. See the explication of it there.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Then came to him certain of the Sadduces <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 23.6.8.</ns0:note> which deny that there is any resurrection and they asked him,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Saying, Master, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 25.5.</ns0:note> Moses wrote unto us, If any mans brother die, having a wife, and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And the second took her to wife, and he died childless.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also. And they left no children, and died.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Last of all the woman died also.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Therefore in the resurrection, whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riage<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riage.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Neither can they die any more; for they are <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 3.2.</ns0:note> equal unto the angels, and are the children of God, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the children of the resurrection.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Now that the dead are raised, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 3.6.</ns0:note> even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 22.23. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and on <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 11.18, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> where all the passages in this <ns0:hi>piece of History</ns0:hi> are fully opened. By <ns0:hi>equal with the Angels,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 36<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> we must not understand in all things, but in the thing mentioned; the number of the <ns0:hi>Elect</ns0:hi> shall be <ns0:hi>per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect</ns0:hi>; so there shall be no need of Marrying, or giving in Marriage, to multiply the number of Men. 2. There shall be no more Marriages amongst Men, than amongst Angels, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 38. <ns0:hi>All live unto God.</ns0:hi> Tho <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> were dead at the speaking of those words, yet they were not so in Gods Eye, who was determined to raise them up in the last Day, and who with the same Eye beholds things past, present, and to come. But see more in the Notes before mentioned.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, thou hast well said.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And after that, they durst not ask him any question at all.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> were the Jewish Doctors of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> Faction, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nemies to the <ns0:hi>Sadduces</ns0:hi>; they applaud our Saviour's answer, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> as the <ns0:hi>Herodians</ns0:hi> before (in the case of the Tribute) so the <ns0:hi>Sadduces</ns0:hi> here are put to silence. He will now put the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> to silence.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And he said unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Math. 22.42. Mark 12.35.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 110.1.</ns0:note> How say they that Christ is Davids son?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And David himself saith, in the book of psalms. The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 Till I make thine enemies thy footstool.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?<ns0:note place="bottom">The answer had been easy if the Scribes and Pharisees, who (<ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith) were there also, had owned Christ to be the Son of God. But this they did not own, and so (as <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> tells us) <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 22.46. <ns0:hi>No Man was able to answer him a Word, neither durst any Man from that Day forth ask him any more questions.</ns0:hi> Thus Christ Nonplust all his Adversaries.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Then in the audience of all the people, he said unto his disciples,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 Which devour widows houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have met with all this before, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 11.43. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 23.6, 7. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 12.38, 39, 40. See the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on those Texts.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
